title: Normalized ordinary and derived coefficient direct-image squares
statement: For abelian categories with their specified (possibly differently sized) derived categories, additive direct-image functors $F,G$ and exact coefficient functors $U,V$, and a specified property $P$ of the ordinary comparison, a normalized square consists of $\alpha:FV\cong UG$ satisfying $P(\alpha)$ and $\beta:RF\,DV\cong DU\,RG$ whose evaluations on every complex intertwine the actual universal right-derived units and the exact localization factor isomorphisms [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For the coefficient models and finite fixed-scalar encodings [def-sfb-integral-ambient-coefficient-presentation], define FinitePushEncoding at level $n+1$ to be this normalized square between the actual ringed finite-coefficient direct image [def-weil-pbc-four-corners] and fixed-scalar pro-etale direct image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Require its ordinary map to be identity on underlying sections. Define AmbientEncoding similarly between the ordinary internal-module direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and the ordinary completed-ring direct image [def-weil-pbc-four-corners], using the specified internal-module equivalences on source and target; require identity on underlying sections. These are data with normalization predicates, not arbitrary actions or arbitrary choices of an isomorphism. The finite square is defined first for an arbitrary adic datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] as FiniteCoefficientPushEncoding, and its specialization to the actual valuation-ring datum is the same FinitePushEncoding; both comparisons are the identical normalized square projection.
